units.text: INT. PYGMALION - CONTINUOUS
Whether he is or not, I’m afraid we shall have some trouble with him.
units.name: PICKERING

units.text: HIGGINS [confidently] Oh no: I think not.
If there’s any trouble he shall have it with me, not I with him.
And we are sure to get something interesting out of him.
About the girl?
units.name: PICKERING

units.text: No. I mean his dialect.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: Oh!
units.name: PICKERING

units.text: PEARCE
units.name: MRS

units.text: at the door.
Doolittle, sir.
units.name: MRS

units.text: She admits Doolittle and retires.
Alfred Doolittle is an elderly but vigorous dustman, clad in the costume of his profession, including a hat with a back brim covering his neck and shoulders.
He has well marked and rather interesting features, and seems equally free from fear and conscience.
He has a remarkably expressive voice, the result of a habit of giving vent to his feelings without reserve.
His present pose is that of wounded honor and stern resolution.
DOOLITTLE [at the door, uncertain which of the two gentlemen is his man] Professor Higgins?
Here. Good morning. Sit down.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: Morning, Governor.
units.name: DOOLITTLE

units.text: He sits down magisterially.
I come about a very serious matter, Governor.
units.name: DOOLITTLE

units.text: HIGGINS [to Pickering] Brought up in Hounslow.
Mother Welsh, I should think. [Doolittle opens his mouth, amazed.
Higgins continues] What do you want, Doolittle?
DOOLITTLE [menacingly] I want my daughter: that’s what I want.
See?
Of course you do. You’re her father, aren’t you? You don’t suppose anyone else wants her, do you? I’m glad to see you have some spark of family feeling left. She’s upstairs. Take her away at once.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: DOOLITTLE [rising, fearfully taken aback] What!
Take her away. Do you suppose I’m going to keep your daughter for you?
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: DOOLITTLE [remonstrating] Now, now, look here, Governor.
Is this reasonable?
Is it fair to take advantage of a man like this?
The girl belongs to me.
You got her.
Where do I come in? [He sits down again].

Your daughter had the audacity to come to my house and ask me to teach her how to speak properly so that she could get a place in a flower-shop. This gentleman and my housekeeper have been here all the time.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: Bullying him.
How dare you come here and attempt to blackmail me? You sent her here on purpose.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: DOOLITTLE [protesting] No, Governor.
You must have. How else could you possibly know that she is here?
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: Don’t take a man up like that, Governor.
units.name: DOOLITTLE

units.text: The police shall take you up. This is a plant—a plot to extort money by threats. I shall telephone for the police
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: he goes resolutely to the telephone and opens the directory.
Have I asked you for a brass farthing? I leave it to the gentleman here: have I said a word about money?
units.name: DOOLITTLE

units.text: HIGGINS [throwing the book aside and marching down on Doolittle with a poser] What else did you come for?
DOOLITTLE [sweetly] Well, what would a man come for?
Be human, governor.
HIGGINS [disarmed] Alfred: did you put her up to it?
So help me, Governor, I never did. I take my Bible oath I ain’t seen the girl these two months past.
units.name: DOOLITTLE

units.text: Then how did you know she was here?
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: DOOLITTLE [“most musical, most melancholy”] I’ll tell you, Governor, if you’ll only let me get a word in.
I’m willing to tell you.
I’m wanting to tell you.
I’m waiting to tell you.

Pickering: this chap has a certain natural gift of rhetoric. Observe the rhythm of his native woodnotes wild. “I’m willing to tell you: I’m wanting to tell you: I’m waiting to tell you.” Sentimental rhetoric! That’s the Welsh strain in him. It also accounts for his mendacity and dishonesty.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: Oh, PLEASE, Higgins: I’m west country myself.
units.name: PICKERING

units.text: To Doolittle.
How did you know the girl was here if you didn’t send her?
units.name: PICKERING

units.text: It was like this, Governor. The girl took a boy in the taxi to give him a jaunt. Son of her landlady, he is. He hung about on the chance of her giving him another ride home. Well, she sent him back for her luggage when she heard you was willing for her to stop here. I met the boy at the corner of Long Acre and Endell Street.
units.name: DOOLITTLE

units.text: Public house. Yes?
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: The poor man’s club, Governor: why shouldn’t I?
units.name: DOOLITTLE

units.text: Do let him tell his story, Higgins.
units.name: PICKERING

units.text: He told me what was up. And I ask you, what was my feelings and my duty as a father? I says to the boy, “You bring me the luggage,” I says—
units.name: DOOLITTLE
